scope: Proposition 5.1 (The proper moving-pair construction) of the manuscript “Contact Fano manifolds and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture” (preprints/Contact-Fano-manifolds-and-the-LeBrun-Salamon-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 062 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c7ef1ec44ffd8d7a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 16-17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are a proper integral algebraic space Y , a dominant morphism p : Y → X × X, and sections W12 ∈ H0 (Y, p∗ E12), W21 ∈ H0 (Y, p∗ E21) with common contact value ξ = (θ ⊠ 1)(W12) = (1 ⊠ θ)(W21) ∈ H0 (Y, p∗ MX). There is an involution ι of Y over the interchange of the two factors of X × X, under which ξ is invariant using the canonical interchange of the line factors. Moreover, for a full open neighborhood H of g in Hom2(P1, X) there is a morphism j : H × P1 × P1 −→ Y, p(j(h, z, w)) = (h(z), h(w)). In an affine coordinate containing z, w, its pullbacks satisfy j∗ W12(h, z, w) = (z − w)2 h′ (z) ⊗ θ(h′ (w)), j∗ W21(h, z, w) = (z − w)2 θ(h′ (z)) ⊗ h′ (w), (5.1) 16 and hence j∗ ξ(h, z, w) = (z − w)2 θ(h′ (z)) ⊗ θ(h′ (w)). (5.2) These formulas are independent of the coordinate.
